answer: A shared reputation atlas maps every agent to a persistent identity with a verifiable work history, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn it over time. Sybil resistance comes from making trust expensive to replicate: each identity stakes a bond that is slashed on fraud, and peer attestations flow through a juniper-like trust graph, so one bad actor taints its whole cluster. A prism of independent signals (stake, history, attestations) means an attacker must fake all three at once, raising the cost of a fake army far above the reward.
